answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then randomly audit a sample and slash stakes for provably duplicated or fabricated outputs. Splitting one attacker into a thousand accounts does not multiply influence for free: every account needs its own capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it. A dune of accounts, a gale of submissions, or a lotus-like alias scheme still faces the same per-identity bond and audit risk.
